samples.summary: `sheets export` writes its progress notice to stdout (console.log), contaminating the stream this change just declared to be "the body callers redirect"
samples.evidence: After `writeFileSync(file, ...)`, line 52-54 does `if (!opts.quiet) { console.log(`Exported to ${file}`); }`. Every other progress notice in the CLI goes to stderr (`io.stderr` in binary.ts:39, content.ts:142, import.ts:144). The change's whole premise (formatter.ts:18-25 and docs/design/cli.md §9) is that stdout carries only the machine-readable body and notices live on stderr; here a non-JSON human line lands on stdout, so `wafflebase sheets export doc out.csv > log` mixes a notice into the body stream. Not touched by the diff, but it is the one remaining stream-assignment inconsistency in the subsystem the change is normalizing.

samples.summary: `sheets cells batch` still casts an arbitrary parsed JSON value to a cell map without validating it is an object
samples.evidence: Line 116-126 declares `let cells: Record<string, unknown>` and assigns `JSON.parse(dataStr)` / the stdin parse directly; line 141 then casts `cells as Record<string, {...} | null>`. `--data 'null'`, `--data '5'` or `--data '[]'` parses fine and is sent verbatim as `{ cells: null }` / `{ cells: 5 }` to `PATCH .../cells`. The diff deliberately reworked this block to route parse failures into the error envelope, but a syntactically-valid non-object still reaches the server (or `printDryRun`) unchecked, so the local envelope the change promises is only produced for a subset of bad input.

samples.summary: `sheets cells batch` with no `--data` blocks on stdin even under `--dry-run`, so a preview hangs on an interactive terminal
samples.evidence: The diff moved the input read inside the try but kept the ordering: `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` (line 122) runs before the `if (opts.dryRun)` check (line 128). On a TTY with no piped input the iteration never completes, so `wafflebase sheets cells batch doc-1 --dry-run` hangs with no output instead of printing the planned request. Other commands check `opts.dryRun` before doing any I/O (cells.ts:47, cells.ts:80, docs.ts:180).

samples.summary: The new last-resort handler flattens every escaped failure to exit code 1, contradicting the documented exit-2 class
samples.evidence: `program.parseAsync().catch((e) => outputError(e))` funnels every unhandled action rejection into `outputError`, which unconditionally sets `process.exitCode = 1` (formatter.ts:57). docs/design/cli.md §10 specifies exit 2 for backend 401/403, 5xx/network, Yorkie attach and font-load failures. Commands that previously escaped as unhandled rejections (e.g. `login`'s timeout/`fetch` failures, which have no try/catch of their own) now report code `ERROR` with exit 1, so callers scripting against the documented 1-vs-2 split cannot distinguish user error from system error on exactly the paths this handler newly covers.

samples.summary: Unconditional `output()` now prints `null`/empty bodies for commands whose responses have no JSON body
samples.evidence: `output(res.data, opts.format)` is now always called; `HttpClient.request` sets `data` to `null` when the response has no parseable body (http-client.ts:139, `res.json().catch(() => null)`), which is the normal case for `DELETE /documents/:id` (docs.ts:154, notes.ts:114, slides.ts:119, api-keys.ts:47). Those commands now emit the literal `null` on stdout (or an empty string under `--format csv`, csv.ts:11) where `--quiet` previously emitted nothing. Not data loss, but `... --quiet > out.json` — the exact scenario the change cites — now writes `null` rather than a usable body for delete-style commands.

finding.summary: Production entrypoint uses `program.parse()` (sync) with async action handlers, so the behavior the new `--quiet` guard asserts via `parseAsync` is not what ships
finding.evidence: `bin.ts:27` calls `program.parse()`, but every registered action is `async function (...)` (e.g. `docs.ts:70`, `cells.ts:16`). Commander only awaits action promises in `parseAsync`; with `parse()` the returned promise is dropped. The new regression guard (`test/output.test.ts:240`) drives `parseAsync`, so it proves the body/error-envelope behavior only for a path the binary never takes. Any action rejection becomes an unhandled rejection (raw Node stack, no `{error:{code,message}}` envelope, exit code not the one `outputError` set), and nothing keeps the process alive until the async action completes. `parseAsync().catch(outputError)` would make the guard faithful.

verdict.reason: The finding's central premise — that bin.ts calls the synchronous program.parse() — is false. packages/cli/src/bin.ts:35-37 already reads `program.parseAsync().catch((e: unknown) => { outputError(e); });`, which is verbatim the fix the reviewer proposes ("parseAsync().catch(outputError) would make the guard faithful"). Line 27, cited as the offending call, is actually `registerSchemaCommand(program);`. The reviewer appears to have mistaken the explanatory comment at bin.ts:28-34 — which describes why parse() would be wrong — for the code itself. A repo-wide grep for `.parse(`/`parseAsync` across packages/cli finds no synchronous program.parse() in any source file; the only other entrypoint, scripts/debug-cmd.mjs:15, also uses parseAsync. Consequently the cited regression guard at test/output.test.ts:240-241 does drive the same code path the binary takes, and test/output.test.ts:303-317 additionally reads src/bin.ts and asserts toContain('program.parseAsync(') and not.toMatch(/program\.parse\s*\(/) plus .catch(/outputError, so the drift described would fail CI. All claimed impacts (unhandled rejections, missing error envelope, wrong exit code, process exiting before async actions complete) are downstream of the false premise.

searchedFor: read cells.ts, sheets-import.ts, docs.ts action bodies for code outside try
finding.summary: `sheets cells batch` parses JSON outside its try/catch, so malformed input escapes the error-envelope path entirely
finding.evidence: `cells.ts:110-120` runs `JSON.parse(dataStr)` and the stdin read/`JSON.parse` before the `try` that starts at line 132. A bad `--data '{'` (or a stdin read error) throws inside the async action, bypassing `outputError`, so no `{error:{code:'ERROR',message:...}}` reaches stderr and `process.exitCode = 1` is never set. Combined with `bin.ts:27`'s `program.parse()` (no `parseAsync`, no `.catch`), it surfaces as an unhandled-rejection trace — exactly the invariant the delta's new test ('prints the error envelope on stderr and exits 1') claims to protect, on a command the guard does not cover.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. In packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts, the batch action's try block opens at line 115, BEFORE any input handling: JSON.parse(dataStr) is at line 118, the stdin `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` loop is at lines 121-124, and JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(...)) is at line 125 — all inside the try, whose `catch (e) { outputError(e); }` is at lines 145-147. A malformed `--data '{'` or a stdin read error is therefore caught and routed through outputError, which writes the {error:{code,message}} envelope to stderr and sets process.exitCode = 1 (formatter.ts:52-58). The comment at cells.ts:110-114 explicitly documents that the read+parse were deliberately placed inside the try for exactly this reason; the reviewer appears to have read that comment as evidence of the defect it describes preventing. The second leg of the claim is also false: bin.ts:35 uses program.parseAsync().catch((e) => outputError(e)), not program.parse() without a catch, so even an escaping rejection would still yield the error envelope and exit 1. Neither element of the claimed bypass path exists.
